Reviewer: independent read-only PowerShell analysis; no build, test, imports, or timing windows

Interpretation.AggregateMethod: median of per-window medians; with two repeats this is their arithmetic mean; each window receives equal weight
Interpretation.NearTieThresholdMeaning: descriptive review threshold, not a significance test; all sign swaps and range overlaps are listed independently of threshold
Interpretation.CrossRepeatMethod: observed slower ours versus observed faster baseline; separated ranges are evidence only for these two windows, not confidence intervals or future worst-case bounds
Interpretation.CorrectnessScope: 160 output tensor comparisons on the final frame of 128 windows, including PyTorch oracle self-comparisons; not 160 models and not every timed frame
Interpretation.ResourceScope: process CPU from cumulative process CPU time; RSS/whole-system CPU/GPU/VRAM are unweighted external sample means; GPU and VRAM are whole device and include desktop/other processes
Interpretation.OrderLimitation: PyTorch CPU runs first for each model; other engines shuffled; model order fixed; frequency, temperature, competing processes, power, and affinity history not recorded
Interpretation.PortabilityLimitation: one CPU, one GPU, fixed 640x640 FP32 batch-1 input; no torch.compile, TensorRT, FP16 or INT8 baseline

Findings: No mismatch found in the complete formal benchmark, current main/CLI/replay DLL, or recorded CPU/GPU oracle evidence.
CPU numerical median-latency winners: .pt 7/8 and ORT 1/8; .pt has separated winner ranges on 6/8. v10n .pt versus ORT differs by only 0.138 percent and the order swaps between repeats.

GPU numerical winners: .pt Vulkan 3/8, ONNX Vulkan 1/8, PyTorch CUDA 4/8, ORT CUDA 0/8. The yolo11n ONNX win is only 0.079 percent versus PyTorch, with a repeat-order swap and overlapping observed ranges.

CPU .pt and ONNX are both faster than PyTorch on all eight models with separated observed ranges. Against ORT, .pt is nominally faster on seven models and separated-faster on six; ONNX is faster on five.
GPU .pt is faster than PyTorch on three models and ONNX on four by aggregate medians, but each has three separated-faster models; both formats are faster than ORT on all eight with separated ranges.

Median CPU time per frame is lower for both CPU formats than both baselines on all eight models, but CPU .pt RSS is higher than both baselines on all eight, and ONNX CPU RSS is higher than ORT on all eight.

Both GPU formats have lower process CPU time and RSS than both baselines on all eight models. Whole-device VRAM sample means are higher for the Vulkan windows; these measurements do not establish per-process VRAM or energy efficiency.

v10n CPU .pt has a marginally lower median than ORT but a higher P95 and near-identical, marginally lower measured throughput. Median-latency winner counts must not be generalized to all performance metrics.
160 benchmark passes are 140 cross-backend output checks plus 20 reference self-checks, on final frames of 128 windows; not 160 independent oracle cases.

ResourceSampling.Note: sampled RSS peaks may miss shorter peaks; low process CPU or high GPU busy percentage alone does not establish energy efficiency
